regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters: IIP overall slipped to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%, and core sector decelerated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%. The quality of growth is narrowing — capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity are doing the heavy lifting, while the composite PMI at 54.6 masks manufacturing's slide to 52.8. Invert the headline: if services PMI at 54.5 softens one more print, the composite drops below 54 and the growth narrative loses its last pillar.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile reading — is the number RBI actually fears, not the headline CPI at 4.45% YoY. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is benign, which creates a dangerous illusion: the MPC can point to core and call itself comfortable while WPI at 9.92% YoY signals producer-price pressure that will feed through to core within two quarters. The RBI's own forecast revision to 5.1% YoY from 4.6% YoY is the tell — they know the headline will worsen before it improves.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits — 75th percentile of the decade range — only partially captures. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% YoY means the wholesale funding market is being leaned on precisely when corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month sits at its lowest historical decile. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% during a rate pause, macro-prudential tightening via risk weights followed within three quarters.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate calculus is shifting: with RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY, the ex-ante real rate is barely positive and shrinking. A rate cut in this environment would be credibility-destroying — fuel at 22.93% YoY and WPI at 9.92% YoY would make any dovish pivot look like capitulation. The RBI is effectively frozen: it cannot cut without inflaming inflation expectations, and it cannot hike without choking a capex cycle that is just finding its footing.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — approaching the 78–80% threshold that historically triggers fresh private capex commitments — is the most genuinely encouraging signal in today's dataset. Credit to industry at 20.0% YoY and credit to services at 22.9% YoY confirm this is being financed, not just announced. The inversion: core sector growth slipping to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% means the upstream inputs — steel, cement, electricity — are not yet confirming the capex acceleration. Watch core sector for two more months before calling the cycle self-sustaining.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month and passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY alongside two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY suggest broad-based demand — but the GST number demands decomposition. At 71st percentile, it is strong but not exceptional, and the FYTD figure at ₹10,42,757 cr sits at only the 14th percentile, suggesting the monthly print is partly base-effect flattery. The vehicle sales data is the cleaner signal: two-wheelers at 19.7% YoY capture rural and semi-urban demand that GST formalization effects can distort. Both are pointing the same direction — consumption is holding, not surging.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month (lowest decile historically) indicates capital markets are not absorbing the overflow.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 FY27 to ease deposit pressure, not inflation. Position for 50-75 bps of cuts by September 2026.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile has preceded either RBI rate cuts or NBFC stress events. Last time CD ratio was this elevated (2022), RBI cut rates 250 bps within 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals strong investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month) — at 74th percentile of 10-year range and approaching the 78-80% threshold that historically triggers fresh capex. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% prior) but still positive. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (up from 6.5% YoY prior) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2% YoY prior) confirm broad-based capex financing.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Domestic equipment manufacturers (Cummins, Escorts, Bharat Heavy Electricals) will see order book acceleration. Infrastructure contractors (L&T, Larsen & Toubro) should see margin expansion as utilisation rises. Avoid cyclical consumer discretionary — capex cycle crowds out consumption credit.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the inflection point where capex typically accelerates. In 2015-2017, similar utilisation levels preceded 3 years of 15%+ capex growth.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (rising 2 consecutive months: 29,845 → 31,961 → 32,297 ₹ cr / month), at 92nd percentile of 10-year range. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn prior month, 82nd percentile). SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (rising 2 consecutive months, 93rd percentile). MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (rising 2 consecutive months, 86th percentile). Equity MF net inflows at 29,329 ₹ cr net / month (up from 24,697 ₹ cr net / month prior). DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (rising 2 consecutive months: 128 → 8,930.1 → 58,502 ₹ cr net / month, 100th percentile).","implication":"SIP AUM growing 40% YoY while SIP accounts growing 25% YoY — average ticket size rising sharply, indicating affluent retail entering, not mass-market expansion. Maintain overweight on Nifty 50 quality names; avoid micro-cap momentum plays.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile have historically preceded market corrections within 6-12 months. In 2021, similar SIP inflow peaks preceded a 20% correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Credibility","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY prior month, 95th percentile of 10-year range) — strongest signal in the dataset. WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78% YoY prior). Brent crude at 102.39 $/bbl (up from 96.1 $/bbl 3 months ago, 71st percentile). Natural gas at 3.015 $/MMBtu (32nd percentile, mild relief). Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY (up from 4.38% YoY prior, 41st percentile) — fuel inflation is the primary driver. RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (up from 4.6% YoY prior).","implication":"RBI's rate-cut cycle is now at risk. If Brent sustains above 105 $/bbl, headline CPI will breach 5% by Q2 FY27, forcing RBI to hold or hike. Hedge long equity positions with long oil calls (Brent 105 strike, 6-month). Avoid refiners (IOCL, BPCL) — margin compression from crude spike. Overweight energy explorers (ONGC) and fertiliser stocks (which benefit from higher crude-linked feedstock costs being passed through).","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has preceded RBI policy reversals. In 2022, similar fuel inflation spikes forced RBI to abandon rate cuts and hike instead.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"Fed Hiking, BOJ Tightening, Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a. prior, rising 2 in a row, 68th percentile). US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.24% yield (down from 5.29% prior but at 95th percentile of 10-year range). BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a. prior, 86th percentile, strong-negative signal score: -72). ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2.0% p.a. prior). US PMI composite at 56 index (up from 54.5 prior, 84th percentile). DXY at 101.918 index (up 4 of last 5 months, 55th percentile). US core CPI at 2.4462% YoY (falling 2 in a row, mild relief).","implication":"BOJ tightening (1% rate, first hike in 17 years) is unwinding the yen carry trade. India's FII flows remain vulnerable — 29,631 ₹ cr net / month is strong but reversible if US yields spike above 5.5%. Hedge long INR positions; consider 6-month USD/INR calls at 97.50 strike.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ at 86th percentile tightening while Fed holds is a rare regime. Last similar divergence (2015-2016) preceded EM currency crises and 15-20% corrections in emerging market equities.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening; RBI Intervention Likely Soon","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 ₹ (down from 96.3 ₹ prior, but up 3 of last 5 months: 95.24 → 94.34 → 95.24 → 96.15 → 95.24 → 96.15 ₹, 91st percentile of 10-year range, strong-negative signal score: -82). FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month prior, but volatile: -114 → -3,111.9 → 29,631 ₹ cr net / month). DXY at 101.918 index (up 4 of last 5 months). US 10-year Treasury at 5.24% yield (95th percentile) — carry trade incentive weakening.","implication":"INR at 96.15 is testing 96.50 support. If breached, RBI will intervene (likely selling USD 2-3 bn / week). FII flows are fragile — any spike in US yields above 5.5% will reverse the 29,631 ₹ cr net / month inflow. Position for INR weakness to 97.00-97.50 ₹/USD by Q2 FY27. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, auto components) who benefit from INR depreciation. Avoid import-heavy sectors (telecom, aviation) until INR stabilises.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness has preceded RBI intervention and 100-150 bps of INR stabilisation within 3 months. In 2022, similar INR weakness triggered RBI's first intervention in 4 years.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Surge Masks GCC Consolidation","data_text":"Office absorption at 21 mn sq ft / quarter (up from 19.8 mn sq ft / quarter prior, rising 2 of last 5 quarters: 13.7 → 13.2 → 5.2 → 13.2 → 21 → 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter, 14th percentile of 10-year range, strong-negative signal score: -72). Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (down from 15.1% prior, 42nd percentile). Nifty IT index flat (recent: 23,447 → 23,141 → 22,780 → 22,716 → 22,620 → 22,422 index, falling 5 in a row). Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (down from 5.0% prior, rising 2 of last 5 quarters, 7th percentile, strong-positive signal score: 86). Rent in Bengaluru at 100.6 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 94 ₹/sqft/mo prior, 57th percentile). Rent in Mumbai at 125 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 117.9 ₹/sqft/mo prior, 38th percentile).","implication":"Office absorption is surging (21 mn sq ft / quarter) but Nifty IT is collapsing (down 5 consecutive months). This decoupling signals that Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — not traditional IT services firms — are the primary office occupiers. GCCs are captive centres for multinational corporates (Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Apple) and are NOT correlated with Indian IT services revenue. This means: (1) Commercial real estate (office) is decoupling from IT services stocks as a proxy; (2) Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are losing relevance as occupiers; (3) Retail mall vacancy at 7th percentile (4.8%) is at a 10-year low, signalling consumer spending resilience despite equity market weakness. FALSIFIABILITY: If office absorption falls below 15 mn sq ft / quarter for 2 consecutive quarters, this thesis breaks. ACTION: Overweight commercial real estate REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) — they are capturing GCC demand, not IT services demand. Underweight traditional IT services; they are structurally losing office footprint to remote work and automation.","pct_10y":14,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 14th percentile is historically weak, but the composition has shifted. GCC occupancy is at a 10-year high while traditional IT services occupancy is at a 10-year low — a structural regime change that equity markets have not yet priced.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Capex Upcycle Meets Inflation Ceiling — RBI Caught in the Middle

The facts:

  • IIP Capital Goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — approaching the 78–80% threshold that historically triggers fresh private investment commitments.
  • But fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) has forced RBI's own forecast up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6% YoY, closing the door on any near-term rate relief.
  • PMI Composite at 54.6 masks manufacturing's slide to 52.8 — services are carrying the expansion; one soft services print ends the story.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY and PV sales at 16% YoY confirm consumption is holding across urban and semi-urban segments.

The tension: The capex cycle needs rate stability or easing to sustain private investment IRRs; fuel inflation at a decade-high percentile makes easing impossible. Growth is accelerating into a policy ceiling it cannot break through.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY for two consecutive months above 6.0% — that is the confirmation that capex is pulling upstream inputs, not just being financed on paper.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Surveys Signal Strength; Bond Market and China Signal Otherwise

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 56 (84th percentile) and Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,239 (100th percentile) price a DM re-acceleration.
  • But US GDP slowed to 2.2% SAAR from 2.5% SAAR, and China GDP decelerated to 4.3% YoY from 5.0% YoY with PMI Composite at 49.5 — in contraction.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.24% yield (95th percentile) is doing the Fed's tightening work; real economy stress is already embedded in the curve.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75% p.a.) is the underappreciated tail — yen carry unwind accelerates as the rate differential compresses.

The tension: DM equity markets are pricing survey-based optimism; nominal GDP deceleration in the US and outright contraction signals in China suggest the surveys are a leading indicator of nothing — or of a soft landing that the bond market has already rejected.

Bottom line: BOJ's next move is the global liquidity trigger to watch — a further hike to 1.25% p.a. would accelerate yen carry unwind and pressure EM flows including India within 60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record Highs; Funding Plumbing Under Stress

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising two consecutive months) and DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile) represent the strongest domestic absorption on record.
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month is positive but volatile — the prior two months were ₹-114 cr and ₹-3,112 cr net / month respectively.
  • But corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (lowest historical decile) signals capital markets are not providing an alternative funding channel as bank deposits lag.
  • MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (86th percentile) is a stock of savings seeking equity returns — but it is not solving the banking system's deposit shortfall.

The tension: Retail savings are flowing into mutual funds at record pace, bypassing the banking system — which is precisely what widens the credit-deposit gap and forces banks toward wholesale funding at higher cost.

Bottom line: Watch deposit growth: a sustained print below 11% YoY for two more months will force RBI's hand on macro-prudential tightening, regardless of the rate stance.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Retail Real Estate Tightens; Office REITs Disconnected from Leasing Reality

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 5 percentage points vs prior period), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY) provide the funding base.
  • Supply is skewed premium: 34% of new launches in the ₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr band and 24% in the ₹1.5–2.5 cr band — developers are chasing NRI and affluent buyers, not mass-market demand.
  • Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (7th percentile) is near a decade low — physical retail is tighter than at any point in the post-COVID recovery.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior prints — REIT investors are pricing office risk that leasing data (21 mn sq ft / quarter absorption) does not yet justify.
  • Nifty 50 at 22,422 has fallen five consecutive sessions; India VIX rising to 14.46 (from 10.35 five months ago) confirms the anxiety is structural, not a single-day event.

The tension: Physical retail is at a decade-low vacancy while office REITs trade as if the leasing cycle is turning — the divergence between asset classes within real estate is as wide as it has been in this cycle.

Bottom line: Overweight physical retail exposure (mall operators, retail-anchored developers) over office REITs until Nifty IT — falling five sessions straight to 22,422 — stabilises and GCC demand visibility improves.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — Fuel and the Carry Unwind

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) — if Brent sustains above $100/bbl, every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill, widening CAD by ~40 bps and pressuring INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) toward 98.
  • BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) — a further hike compresses the yen carry trade, triggering EM outflows; FII flows already showed two months of net selling before this month's ₹29,631 cr net / month reversal.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with corporate bond issuance at a decade-low ₹18,700 cr / month — if deposit growth stays at 10.8% YoY while credit runs at 17.1% YoY, NBFC funding costs rise and the weakest borrowers reprice first.
  • Nifty 50 falling five consecutive sessions to 22,422 with India VIX at 14.46 — a break below 22,000 would trigger passive outflows and test DII absorption capacity at current SIP run-rates.

The tension: Fuel inflation and the BOJ are external risks that RBI cannot offset with domestic tools; the CD ratio and equity correction are domestic risks that compound if the external shocks materialise simultaneously.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a close above $105/bbl makes the RBI's 5.1% YoY inflation forecast untenable and forces a hawkish pivot that the equity market is not priced for.

"}
